Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort.

Students today spend long hours studying, attending classes, using digital devices, and participating in sports or extracurricular activities. Clear vision is essential, making many students choose between contact lenses and LASIK surgery.

Contact lenses offer temporary vision correction, but they require daily cleaning, proper hygiene, and ongoing maintenance. Extended wear can sometimes lead to dryness, irritation, and an increased risk of eye infections.

• Freedom from daily lens maintenance

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active
• Avoiding tobacco use
• Scheduling regular eye check-ups

Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort.

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active

👁️ Diabetes is under control… but is your vision?

Diabetes can affect more than just your blood sugar—it can also silently damage the retina, leading to Diabetic Macular Oedema (DMO), a common cause of vision loss in people with diabetes.

The early stages of DMO often have no noticeable symptoms, making regular retinal screening essential.

Watch for warning signs such as:
✔️ Blurred vision
✔️ Difficulty reading
✔️ Distorted straight lines
✔️ Faded colours
✔️ Dark spot in the centre of your vision

The good news is that early diagnosis and timely treatment can help preserve your sight.

If you have diabetes, schedule a comprehensive retinal examination every year, even if your vision seems normal.


Protect your vision—because seeing well is an important part of living well with diabetes.

A Proud Milestone for Globus Eye Org (GEO) Specialist EyeCare

We are delighted to share that Dr. Eesha Shukla-Gokhale, Consultant Ophthalmologist at Globus Eye Org (GEO) Specialist EyeCare, Goregaon, was invited to serve as an International Examiner for the Part 2 FRCOphth Examination conducted by the Royal College of Ophthalmologists (UK) in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

🔴 Red Eye? It May Not Be Just an Infection.

Many people assume that a red eye is caused by an infection or allergy. However, in some cases, it may be a sign of uveitis—inflammation inside the eye that can threaten vision if left untreated.

Watch out for symptoms such as:
✔ Eye redness
✔ Eye pain
✔ Sensitivity to light
✔ Blurred vision

Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to prevent complications and protect your eyesight.

If you are experiencing persistent redness or any of these symptoms, don’t ignore them. A comprehensive eye examination can help identify the cause and ensure timely treatment.

At Globus Eye Org, our specialists provide expert diagnosis and management of uveitis and other inflammatory eye conditions.

Cataract surgery is one of the safest and most successful eye procedures, but achieving the best visual outcome starts with proper pre-surgical planning.

Before your surgery, make sure you discuss these important checks with your eye specialist:

✅ Detailed Eye Measurements (Biometry)
✅ Dry Eye Assessment & Treatment
✅ Review of Medical Conditions & Medications
✅ Retina, Macula & Glaucoma Evaluation

These evidence-based assessments help improve surgical planning, optimize visual outcomes, and ensure realistic expectations after surgery.

Ocular Sarcoidosis: Protecting Your Vision Through Early Diagnosis 👁️

Did you know that sarcoidosis can affect the eyes and, in some patients, eye inflammation may be the first sign of the disease?

Ocular sarcoidosis can present with blurred vision, floaters, eye redness, light sensitivity, or recurrent episodes of uveitis. If left untreated, it can lead to complications such as cataract, glaucoma, macular edema, and permanent vision loss.

At Globus Eye Org, our uveitis specialists provide comprehensive evaluation and evidence-based management of ocular inflammatory diseases. Diagnosis often requires collaboration with rheumatologists, pulmonologists, and physicians to assess for systemic involvement.

Treatment is individualized and may include:
• Steroid eye drops
• Oral medications
• Periocular or intraocular injections
• Immunomodulatory therapy
• Biologic agents in selected patients

Early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary approach offer the best chance of preserving vision and improving long-term outcomes.

If you are experiencing persistent eye redness, floaters, blurred vision, or recurrent eye inflammation, schedule a comprehensive eye examination with a uveitis specialist.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a very disappointing experience with Dr. Anurag Agrawal at Jain Hospital after my mother’s cataract surgery in February.

We have visited the doctor multiple times since the operation, but every time only eye drops are changed with no proper diagnosis or solution provided. We are repeatedly told that the surgery was done perfectly, while my mother is still struggling daily and suffering physically.

As patients, we trust doctors with our loved ones and spend hard-earned money hoping for genuine care and treatment. It is extremely painful and frustrating to see no improvement despite so many follow-ups.

Based on our experience, I would not recommend this clinic or treatment. I hope other families do proper research before making such important medical decisions.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We are genuinely sorry to hear that your mother is experiencing discomfort and understand how concerning this situation can be for any family member.

Visual recovery after cataract surgery can sometimes be influenced by multiple factors beyond the surgery itself.

As you have yourself mentioned that the doctor has repeatedly confirmed that the surgery was performed successfully, we humbly request that instead of assuming negligence or poor treatment, it may be worthwhile to further investigate possible causes of persistent symptoms.

We suggest considering the following:

• Ensure post-operative medicines and instructions are being followed exactly as advised
• Consider detailed retinal and corneal evaluation if not already done for any other causes
• Seek additional investigations for headaches or neurological causes if recommended
• Share complete medical history and previous eye conditions, as these can influence recovery outcomes

Our intention has always been to provide the best possible care, and we remain open to discussing concerns constructively to help find a solution rather than leaving unresolved suffering.

We sincerely wish your mother a speedy recovery and better health. Take Care!
